output: The Helan Mountains, sometimes called a "mountain island in the sky," separate the semi-arid Ordos Plateau and the Yellow River Valley from the desert of the Alxa Plateau to the west. Like the mountain ranges of the Great Basin in western North America, the Helan Range holds isolated stands of dense conifer forest and may support endemic plant and animal communities. Scientists have paid the ecoregion little attention, but it is known to shelter several rare species, including blue sheep, blue-eared pheasants, and the endemic Helan pika. Commercial logging is still destroying habitat and threatens the region's high biodiversity.

We are working to cut operational costs further by developing an ultra-high efficiency InGaN solar cell. [2] Changing the ratio of indium to gallium in the film tunes the band gap anywhere from 0.7eV to 3.4eV. That lets us build a multi-layered structure that captures the entire solar spectrum, so our InGaN cells can convert a much larger share of the sun's light energy into electricity.

The research has two phases. In the first, we will characterize InGaN and study how it behaves as a semiconductor. In the second, we will use that data to decide how many layers to stack and what concentrations of indium and gallium each layer should contain. Getting those choices right will maximize light absorption and, above all, electricity generation.

# Conservation of nose-touch avoidance across *C. elegans* and relatives

Nose-touch avoidance was conserved in five of the six species tested (Figure 5A). The exception was *C. tripartitum*: after the first few positive trials, its overall avoidance rate fell below 10%, which suggests it adapts to the stimulus faster than *C. elegans* and the other species (Figure 5A). In the first three trials, though, *C. tripartitum* responded at a level quantitatively similar to *C. elegans* (Figure S2 in Additional file 2).

In the five species that responded to nose touch, ablating the ASH neurons abolished avoidance (Figure 5A). Four of these species still responded in 20 to 30% of trials after ablation. ASH-ablated *Caenorhabditis* sp. 3 animals did not respond to nose touch at all (Figure 5A).

Ablating the AWC neuron had no effect on the nose-touch response in any of the species (Figure S3 in Additional file 2).

The alitrunk (Fig. 15) is conspicuously swollen and sits well above the level of the propodeal dorsum. The propodeum has a pair of strong spines, straight to slightly upcurved. There is no metanotal groove, and the metapleural lobes are triangular and conspicuous. In profile, the petiole has an elongate peduncle and a well-developed node whose dorsum slopes down posteriorly, so the posterior face is short. The anterior and dorsal surfaces of the postpetiole form a single convexity, and the posterior face is truncated. In dorsal view, both the petiolar and postpetiolar nodes are broader than long.

The dorsum of the head is strongly longitudinally rugose, with 5 to 7 rugae between the frontal carinae at eye level. These rugae are irregular and meander slightly, and a few anastomoses are usually present. The scrobal area is mostly smooth but typically has 1 or 2 fine rugulae crossing it just behind the antennal fossa. Behind the eyes, the sides of the head are finely reticulate-rugose, and this sculpture continues around the posterior margins of the scrobe to the occiput. The spaces between the rugae are unsculptured or show at most the faintest superficial traces. The dorsal alitrunk is finely but strongly reticulate-rugose throughout, with broad, shining interspaces. The petiole dorsum is rugulose, while the postpetiole ranges from rugulose to only faintly sculptured. The gaster is unsculptured.

All dorsal surfaces of the head and body are densely covered with fine, acute hairs. Color is dark reddish brown to blackish brown.

Subject: Findings on foxl2 expression patterns in trout

Dear Customer,

Here is a summary of what we found on foxl2 transcript expression in your study.

Both foxl2 transcripts are expressed very early in development (Figure 2). In the male, foxl2a expression was highly restricted, while the diverged paralog foxl2b was present in most of the adult extragonadal tissues we examined (see Additional file 2).

In adult female tissues, by contrast, foxl2b expression was highly restricted, essentially confined to the skin, gill, and ovary. foxl2b expression in the testis was very strong. This fits earlier work showing foxl2b present and foxl2a absent in later stages of testis development in trout [23].

These results suggest that foxl2b may regulate male-specific genes such as cyp19b1, particularly later in development.

Thank you for your time and interest in our research.

Best regards,

[Your Name]

Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) cannot back carbon neutrality claims for electricity use beyond what the claimant's meter records, because most RECs come from projects that were financially viable without selling them. [10] Those RECs lack additionality. Additionality asks a counterfactual question: what would have happened under the status quo if no one had bought or contracted for the REC? There are many ways to test for it, but they all come down to whether the project needed REC revenue to survive financially. Unless additionality is verified, a REC is not equivalent to a real emissions offset.

We derived a time-dependent mild-slope equation from the formal derivation of Smith & Sprinks (1975) and used it to obtain a higher-order dispersion relation for waves over an uneven bottom.

Using only linear dispersion for steady waves, we recovered equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), known as the Modified Mild-Slope Equation (MMSE). At leading order, the modified curvature terms of the MMSE have significant effects, while the slope-squared terms remain negligible, as the mild-slope assumption implies. We therefore kept all the modified curvature terms that the MSE neglects, which gives a uniform model.

We then built a finite element (FEM) model to predict wave scattering by a varying bottom. The uniform model generally captures the main features of waves over different sea beds, including sinusoidal beds and man-made bars. For sinusoidal beds, it agrees more closely with experimental data than other established models. For man-made bars, both the MMSE and the uniform model agree more closely with experimental data than Kirby (1986) does.

The FEM model can also be applied to wave transformation over arbitrarily varying bathymetry.

The myth in the Phaedrus is more intense than any of the earlier descriptions, though it belongs to a different realm. It concerns a former existence rather than a future one. It shows a conflict between reason, backed by passion or righteous indignation, and the animal instincts. The human soul has traveled in the company of some god and seen truth in the form of the universal before birth, and our present life is the result of a struggle that took place earlier. This world is relative, and we often project it into a future, in the same way that we wonder where men were before they were born or what happens to them after death. The question "Where were men before birth?" sounds strange and unnatural to us, yet it has been as influential and as widespread as the other. In the Phaedrus, the "spiritual combat" of this life is only a figure of speech. The grandeur and force of the whole passage, especially the opening that begins "The mind through all her being is immortal," can be rendered only poorly in another language.

The case is complicated. Google has challenged the validity of this patent and has also filed a separate action against the European Patent Office. The outcome could change how search results behave.

Subject: A note on Buraq

Dear Friend,

People once lived in a world where reality and myth ran together. A clear line between them only appeared with modern comparative biology. Science still has not done away with the in-between zone where a figure like Buraq lives, and we need figures like her to connect empirical knowledge with spiritual experience.

Today she links rationalist taxonomies to what remains of myth's power. You can see this most strongly in the Islamic transport industry, where Buraq, who combines piety and speed, keeps turning up as a kind of patron saint. Airlines from Libya to Indonesia carry her name, and so do bus companies, freight ships, motorcycle taxis, a space camp, an engineering college, and even Pakistan's first drone.

Because her image and her name are so fluid, businesses can bend her to almost any use. She presides over wings and wheels, and she also sells plastic and PVC, heavy metal, heavy-duty diesel (BURAQ LUBRICANTS), Indian food, and surgical instruments.

With appreciation for your curiosity,

In the mid-1860s, King's Cross station expanded north, and its tracks cut through St. Pancras Old Church, the oldest Christian worship site in London. Thomas Hardy, then working as an architect, was given the job of clearing the land. He exhumed the dead with care and arranged their gravestones in a spiral around a central tree. The tree is still standing, but its roots have started to grow around the stones, and the inscriptions are getting harder to read. Other notable figures are buried elsewhere in the cemetery. One monument marks the grave of Mary Wollstonecraft, who wrote *A Vindication of the Rights of Woman* (1792) and was the mother of Mary Shelley, author of *Frankenstein* (1818). Nearby is a large mausoleum inscribed with the name Sir John Soane. It commemorates the collector and architect whose eccentric house still stands on Lincoln's Inn Fields, as recorded in the *Description of the House and Museum of Sir John Soane* (1835).

MapleStory monsters: a survival guide

MapleStory has thousands of monsters. Here's where they live and how to survive them.

The weak monsters are the most common and live near towns. They wander aimlessly, and even if you bump into them they won't pay you any attention. You'll take some damage from the contact, but it's nothing to worry about. The most lethal monsters live deep in dungeons.

Monsters ignore you until you attack them or cast a debuff on them. Either one will "aggro" the monster: you get its attention, and it tries to attack you back.

Most enemies attack by running into you over and over. The easiest response is to keep attacking them, since your attacks usually have enough knockback to hold them in place. Sometimes you'll need to jump over them to dodge their attacks entirely.

Cell motility drives embryonic development and plays a part in many physiological and disease processes. When its regulation fails, the results can be severe, ranging from developmental defects to metastatic cancer.

My research aims to uncover the basic mechanisms that control how cells move and change shape. Directed migration requires the cell to remodel its cytoskeleton continuously in response to extracellular signals, some diffusible and some bound to surfaces.

This ecoregion covers the moist deciduous forests that surround the montane rainforests of the northern Western Ghats, in the Indian states of Maharashtra and Karnataka. The land has its origins in Gondwana. During the Cretaceous, the Deccan Plate broke away from Gondwanaland, drifted north, and eventually joined the Eurasian continent. We want to share some information about early hearing development. People usually learn to speak within the first few years of life. Hearing impairment can prevent a child from learning to speak, and it can also make it hard to understand spoken language.

By the time anyone notices that a severely hearing-impaired (deaf) child has a hearing deficit, communication problems may already have caused trouble in the family and held back the child's social skills. These problems are smaller if the child belongs to a Deaf community that uses sign language instead of spoken language (see our article on Deaf Culture).

Many developed countries test hearing in the newborn period so that a deaf child is not unintentionally isolated within a hearing family. Sign language is a complete means of communication, but literacy ultimately depends on understanding speech, because most written languages use symbols to code the sound of each word.

Someone who heard well enough to learn to speak and read keeps the ability to read even if their hearing later becomes too poor to hear voices. A person who never heard well enough to learn to speak, though, rarely reads proficiently (see [4]). Most evidence suggests that a child with very insensitive hearing has the best chance of learning spoken language well when the hearing impairment is identified early. Listening also matters when learning a second language.

Large, soft armchairs, full and ample draperies, eiderdown cushions, and all the other comforts that we alone of the European family understood led only to the imprisonment of their owners. If you had the misfortune to live in a spacious hotel set back within a courtyard, away from the odious noise and smells of the street, you had your throat cut. Treating elegant manners that way put them out of fashion, and people quickly gave them up. In the nervous system, transduction is the process of converting stimuli into electrical signals. In sensory transduction, specialized sensory receptors take physical or chemical inputs and turn them into electrical impulses that travel to the brain.

The visual system is one example. In the retina, rod and cone cells link the physical environment to neural signaling. When light strikes these photoreceptors, it causes a conformational change in the protein rhodopsin. That change starts a cascade of events that alters the photoreceptor's electrochemical gradient. As the gradient falls, the electrical signals sent to the brain decrease as well. So more light hitting the photoreceptor produces fewer electrical impulses, and the brain decodes the visual scene from that signal.

Subject: Tips for hitchhiking in the Ruhr Area, Germany

Dear Customer,

The Ruhr Area (German: Ruhrgebiet), often just called the Ruhr, is an urban region in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is made up of many former industrial cities, including Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna, and Witten.

About five million people live there, far more than in Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich. The region has a dense motorway network, but the tangle of minor roads makes hitchhiking hard. The main motorways are the A1, A2, and A3.

If you hitch here, stay on those three. The smaller roads carry very little transit traffic, so getting anywhere on them is extremely difficult. Germany is generally a pleasant country for hitchhiking, but the Ruhr is by far the worst part of it. Hitching inside the Ruhr is like hitching in a big city such as Istanbul. The cities are independent, but to a traveler they feel like districts of one huge city.

We hope this helps you plan a safe and enjoyable trip.

Mobile gaming and co-creation

Mobile internet is widening what storytelling can do. It makes possible electronic games that run on portable, location-aware interfaces. These games are the latest step in a decades-long line of electronic games that treat the player as an avatar in a gameworld and also as a co-author working alongside the original designers.

With location-aware interfaces, players can bring places in the physical world into their gameworld, and the gameworld into those places. No earlier interactive medium could do this. Mobile games also give players a hand in worldmaking, and they drop linear narratives in favor of cooperative storytelling that depends on how the player experiences a place.

The idea of the "author-player" building a world is not new. What mobile games change is the reach of that process, which no longer stops at the limits of traditional video games. Once worldmaking extends past the screen into the physical world, location-aware interfaces can use the player's sensory experience of real places as a storytelling tool.

In our essay, we theorize the storytelling potential specific to mobile games. We also describe what happened when we tried to put that potential to work by designing and implementing our hybrid-reality game, University of Death.

Subject: Study results: lung tissue volume and aeration analysis

Dear Customer,

Below are the findings from our analysis of lung tissue volume and functional changes.

We calculated total lung tissue volume as the number of voxels multiplied by the volume of one voxel, for compartments with a CT number above zero.

The change in functional residual capacity caused by PEEP withdrawal (ΔFRC) is the difference in total gas volume in the whole lung between PEEP and ZEEP. Alveolar derecruitment is the difference in gas volume within poorly aerated and nonaerated regions between the same two conditions.

We also computed how gas volume changed after PEEP withdrawal in normally aerated regions alone, defined as CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2).

Each patient's lung morphology, meaning the distribution of lost aeration, was classified as diffuse, patchy, or lobar from the distribution of CT attenuations at ZEEP, following the method in reference [21].
